subject: Log retention cutover & evidence pack for MediCore migration
messages:
From: Oliver Hayes <oliver.hayes@medicore.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: security@medicore.com
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Log retention cutover — evidence package request

Hi Aditya,

Thanks for taking this on. As part of MediCore's compliance review for our upcoming data platform migration, our security team needs concrete evidence around Redwood's log retention and deletion processes for the dataset we send (patient-messaging logs). Specifically:

- Snapshot of log retention configuration for the last 12 months (what TTLs are applied where).
- Sample deletion/audit log showing a complete erasure flow for a single tenant (redacted).
- SOC 2 / SIG references that map to log collection, retention, and deletion controls.

We are working against a hard cutover on DEC 10 and would like artifacts by Nov 30 to include in our packet. If any of this requires a customer-specific exception (e.g., longer retention for a subset), flag it explicitly.

Can you confirm scope and an ETA?

Appreciate it —
Oliver
Senior Security Engineer
MediCore Inc
[attachment: medicore_request_summary.pdf (PDF, 48KB)]

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Hayes <oliver.hayes@medicore.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 12:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Log retention cutover — evidence package request

Oliver —

Thanks for the clear list. We can provide the items you requested. High-level responses / plan below:

1) Retention snapshot: we will generate a retention matrix (per-bucket / per-log-type) exported from our config store. Expect a CSV that shows system defaults and any per-tenant overrides.

2) Deletion/audit sample: we'll redact tenant identifiers and provide an end-to-end deletion trace (request -> background job -> S3 object removal -> Audit log entry). This will be a text export (low risk).

3) Controls mapping: our SOC 2 report sections relevant to logging and deletion + the SIG (v2026) answers that map to these controls.

To be safe, we have one clarifying question: does MediCore need proofs of cryptographic key destruction for archived snapshots, or is audit evidence of object deletion sufficient?

ETA: I will drop the retention matrix and a deletion sample by Nov 30. Controls mapping and supporting SOC 2 excerpts will follow on Dec 2. If you need the full SOC 2 report earlier, we can arrange an NDA flow with our legal team.

Next steps: I'll circulate a short mutual action plan (shared Drive) with deliverables and dates.

Best,
Aditya
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
[attachment: log-retention-matrix.csv (CSV, stub)]

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 08:32:00 -0800
Subject: FW: Log retention cutover — evidence package request

Aditya / Grace —

Looping you both in on the deliverables. Operational notes and actions:

- Grace: please generate the retention matrix export and include columns for: log_type, default_ttl, tenant_override, storage_backend, encryption_kms_key_id, last_modified_by, modified_at. Put the CSV in the MediCore Drive folder and mark as confidential.

- Grace / Infra: capture a deletion flow for a test tenant. Steps: create test objects, trigger delete API, wait for background job, confirm S3 object removal and present the audit entry (include s3 object key prefixes and eventIDs). Use sanitized IDs.

- Legal/PS: if MediCore requests extended retention for a subset, we need a retention-exception-form filled and routed to legal. Aditya: please confirm if they already asked for an extension so we can prioritize.

Timing: target internal completion Nov 29 so Aditya can deliver on the 30th.

Thanks —
Laura
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Can Redwood support a customer-scoped exception to extend TTL from 90 to 180 days for the tenant scope "medi-core-prod" only? If so, please initiate the retention-exception-form and route to legal.
